reviewBoundary: Three original senior third-person fifteen-gap clozes. Fictional dog adoption, charity auction and sculpture exhibition. Same-author context and all-key/all-alternative review, shuffled choices, not independent calibration.

units.title: A walk without the ball
units.alignmentNote: One complete original fifteen-gap four-choice narrative following National I. Old source is a level/family drafting reference only.

materials.title: A walk without the ball
materials.text:
When Sam's family adopted a dog named Fern, he bought a bright ball and planned long games in the park. Fern, however, stayed close to her bed. Whenever Sam approached quickly with the ball, she moved ____1____.

Sam felt rejected. He had expected a new companion, not a dog who seemed afraid of his ____2____. His mother reminded him that the shelter had advised a quiet beginning and familiar routines.

For several days, Sam sat nearby with a book instead of trying to start a game. He spoke softly and let Fern choose whether to come ____3____. Once, she rested her head beside his shoe. Sam resisted the urge to make a sudden ____4____.

Their first short walk was not the adventure he had imagined. Fern stopped often to smell the same patch of grass. Sam wanted to ____5____, but his mother asked him to give her time while keeping the lead secure.

At home, Fern returned to the mat by the door. Sam placed the ball nearby, then left it alone. That evening, he heard a soft ____6____. The ball rolled across the floor, pushed by Fern's nose.

Their first game lasted less than a minute. Sam did not ____7____ it by following her when she went back to rest. He was beginning to understand that enthusiasm could become pressure if it left no room for the other creature's ____8____.

Weeks later, Fern carried the ball to him herself. By then, Sam had learned to enjoy more than the ____9____ parts of having a dog: the quiet company, the repeated walks and the small signs of ____10____.

He still loved playing. But he no longer treated a game as something Fern ____11____ him because he had bought a toy. The ball had become an ____12____, not a demand. Sometimes she accepted it; sometimes she preferred to lie nearby. Sam could recognise both as ways of being ____13____. The companion he had wanted was arriving, just more ____14____ than his plan had allowed. This time, he was happy to ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: Fern withdraws from a quick approach, moving away. Forward contradicts that avoidance; upstairs/outside are unsupported destinations.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: Sam intends friendly companionship, so Fern seems afraid of his friendship. Absence/homework/silence do not name his offered interaction.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: Fern chooses whether to approach closer. Early/late concern timing and alone company, not reduced distance.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: A sudden movement could disturb the cautious approach. Promise, journey and purchase do not describe the restrained bodily action.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: Repeated smelling slows the walk, making Sam want to hurry. Sleep, hiding and swimming are not the impatience about pace.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: The rolling ball makes a soft sound. No speech, song or knock at a door is described.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: He does not prolong the game by following a resting dog. The game has already begun and he remembers/watches it; the issue is extending it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Leaving space for Fern’s choice contrasts with pressure. Owner, bed and food do not name voluntary participation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Games are exciting; the new appreciation includes quiet routines. Expense/difficulty/noise do not give the intended contrast with calm companionship.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: Gradual approach and voluntarily bringing a ball signal trust. Anger and hunger are not shown; speed is the opposite of the slow adjustment.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: A toy purchase does not mean the dog owes him a game. Taught, sold and showed do not express the imagined obligation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: The ball offers an invitation that can be accepted or declined. Order is a demand, obstacle blocks and experiment does not express the social offer.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: Playing or quietly lying nearby are both ways to be together. Absence/loss/separation contradict nearby companionship.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: The developing companionship arrives gradually over weeks. Loudness, cost and carelessness do not describe its pace.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: Sam accepts the gradual pace and is happy to wait. Complaining, leaving and competing contradict that patience.

units.title: The cake that was sold twice
units.alignmentNote: One complete original fifteen-gap four-choice narrative following National I. Old source is a level/family drafting reference only.

materials.title: The cake that was sold twice
materials.text:
Leah helped at a village charity auction. She carried items forward while the organiser invited ____1____. Then came a large fruit cake.

An older man offered twenty pounds. A woman bid twenty-five; he offered thirty. Leah worried that the bidding would become ____2____. Instead, the man laughed when the woman finally won.

As Leah carried the cake towards her, the woman asked whether she could leave it at the front. "Please sell it ____3____," she said. "I support the repairs, but cannot eat a whole cake."

Leah hesitated. She had never heard of a buyer giving the purchase ____4____ before collecting it. The organiser checked her intention, then reopened the bidding.

This time, several people joined in with smaller offers. A family bought the cake and asked whether they could ____5____ it immediately. The organisers supplied plates and a knife.

Soon, slices were travelling down the tables. The older man received one and thanked the family. Leah noticed that the first ____6____ had not made him bitter. 

Afterwards, she asked the woman why she had bid if she did not want the cake. "I wanted the roof repaired," she replied. "The cake was a ____7____ of helping."

Leah had been watching the auction as a contest between buyers. The answer reminded her of its wider ____8____. It also brought neighbours together.

While she washed plates, volunteers counted donations. Generosity did not remove the need to check the ____9____. The organiser recorded both sales clearly, so the total could be explained.

Next time, Leah listened to why people ____10____. Some wanted a useful item, some a small pleasure, and some a chance to ____11____. The same action could contain different intentions. Her job was not to ____12____ them from a raised hand alone. When another cake appeared, she smiled but made no ____13____. It might be taken home, shared, or offered again. What happened would depend on the people, not merely on the ____14____. An auction, she realised, could end with more than one kind of ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: An auction organiser invites bids. Recipes and repairs are not price offers; plates carry food.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: Leah fears competitive bidding might turn unfriendly, contrasted with laughter. Silence/invisibility do not describe tension and ordinary is not a feared hostile result.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: The buyer requests a second sale, so again. Secrecy, cheapness and outside location are not her instruction.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Giving the purchase back returns it to the auction for another sale. Out, down and off do not express that return.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: Immediate slices passed around show sharing. Hiding, returning and freezing do not create the communal snack.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: He lost the first bidding but remains cheerful. A slice is welcome, and price/plate do not name the competitive setback.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: The cake is a means of helping fund repairs. Proof/record document something; promise commits to a future action, not the vehicle used for the donation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Repairs and community are the event’s purpose. Price is an offer, audience attendees and schedule timing, not the reason for the auction.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Donations and both sales require checking figures. Recipes, weather and costumes are not the financial record.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: The narrator listens to why people take part. Leaving, complaining and sleeping do not cover the varied positive bidding motives described.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: Contribute expresses helping fund the repairs, the woman’s stated reason. Escape, perform and travel are not the charitable purpose revealed by the conversation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: A raised hand alone cannot establish a motive, so guessing is rejected. Hearing, recording and respecting can be appropriate after the person explains.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: She no longer assumes what a cake’s buyer intends. Mistake/sound/difference do not name the withheld prediction.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: The people determine what happens beyond the object being sold. Roof is the cause, while family/organiser are themselves people rather than the contrasted item.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: The bidder, recipients and repaired community can all be winners. Question, price and recipe do not name the broader beneficiary idea.

units.title: The empty space at the exhibition

materials.title: The empty space at the exhibition
materials.text:
The sculpture arrived a day late. Mara had assumed a plan would bring every exhibit to its ____1____ place. An empty plinth challenged her confidence.

The artist called to apologise. A transport fault had caused the ____2____; the work was safe and would arrive the following morning. Cancelling would disappoint visitors, but pretending nothing was missing was equally ____3____.

Mara discussed the problem with the artist. With his permission, she placed a small photograph beside the plinth and a notice explaining the absence. She also displayed his drawing of the work at an earlier ____4____.

At the opening, visitors stopped there longer than she expected. Some compared the drawing with the photograph; others asked about the material or ____5____ used to join its parts. The missing object made them imagine its size in the room.

One visitor suggested leaving the plinth empty permanently. Mara smiled but ____6____. The questions were interesting, yet they did not make the actual sculpture ____7____. Its weight, surface and relation to a moving viewer could not be fully supplied by a picture.

After delivery, she kept the drawing and an updated explanation. Visitors could see the finished work as well as a little of its ____8____. The delay had prompted a useful addition, but she did not claim that a transport failure had been a brilliant curatorial ____9____.

The artist appreciated that distinction. An accidental difficulty had been handled ____10____; it had not become evidence that difficulties should be manufactured.

Mara's later plans included more space for the stages behind a finished object. They also included careful delivery checks. Learning from an interruption did not require ____11____ it. She had found a way to acknowledge a gap without allowing the gap to ____12____ the whole event. The empty plinth had invited attention, but the sculpture deserved more than being the ____13____ to a puzzle. When she finally walked around it, she was relieved to feel something no photograph had conveyed: the way its forms changed as she ____14____. The room was ready, and the conversation could now ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: The plan assigns each work a place. Secrecy/distance/duration do not establish its intended position as directly.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: The transport fault causes delay, while the sculpture itself remains safe. Exhibition, sculpture and permission are not the interrupted timing.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: Pretending the absence away is unacceptable alongside cancellation’s costs. It is not unavoidable—honest explanation is available—and popularity/efficiency do not address integrity.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: The drawing shows an earlier stage of making. Price is not developmental, location a place and opening the event rather than the object’s development.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: Technique used to join its parts is a making method. A schedule, audience or ticket is not a joining technique.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: Mara rejects permanent absence because the real sculpture remains necessary, so declined. Agreement conflicts with that; celebration/disappearance do not answer the suggestion.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: Questions do not make the real object unnecessary: physical qualities still matter. Fragility, expense and permanence are not the challenged need for its presence.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: The earlier drawing shows development behind the finished work. Absence was temporary, ownership and popularity are not the making process.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: A curatorial strategy is a deliberately designed approach; Mara refuses to rebrand an accident as one. Contract, complaint and expense do not name that intentional approach.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: She creates useful explanation from a difficulty, handling it constructively. Secrecy and carelessness contradict honesty/care; automatic action lacks the deliberate discussion.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: Learning from a failure does not require repeating or manufacturing it. Hiding is rejected by explanation, forgetting by retained learning, and measuring does not create another failure.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: She prevents the absence defining the entire event. Explanation and records are useful, filling the gap is the later delivery, not the dominating effect being resisted.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: A sculpture is more than the answer to the temporary puzzle of its absence. Cause/cost/title do not express the reduced riddle-solving role.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: Walking around changes the viewer’s moving viewpoint and apparent forms. Waiting, speaking and planning do not change position in the described experience.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: Arrival allows the discussion to continue with the actual work. Stopping/vanishing end it, and repeat denies development from the earlier questions.
